# C02: 2017 client PDB (facts for other items)

`Files/Client/2017/Fiesta.pdb` is the full private PDB of the 2017 client `Files/Client/2017/Fiesta.bin`
(`patch_2017_08_p01`). It is **not** the 2016 build we reconstruct. Everything taken from it is evidence
level *(pdb2017)* until a 2016 binary agrees (same opcode in a handler table, same size check, same field
use). This file says what was ported, how far it agrees with 2016, and what each item should follow up.

## 1. Tools and generated files

| What | Where | Regenerated by |
|---|---|---|
| PDB reader (types, publics, layouts) | `tools/protocol-re/pdb.py` (`selftest` asserts known facts) | – |
| Opcode → official name + flattened `PROTO_*` layout | `docs/protocol/pdb-layouts.json` | `regen.sh` (`pdb.py … layouts`) |
| Verdicts for 2016-vs-2017 name conflicts | `docs/protocol/pdb-name-verdicts.json` (hand-made, C02) | – |
| 2017 client in Ghidra, PDB applied | `re-data/ghidra/client2017.gpr`, export `re-data/exports/client2017/` (`decomp.c`, `strings.tsv`, `functions.tsv`) | headless import, see §8 |
| Call graph of both clients | `re-data/exports/{client,client2017}/functions.tsv` (entry, size, full name, callees) | `tools/protocol-re/ExportFuncs.java` |
| 2016 client names ported from 2017 | `tools/protocol-re/names/client/C02.json` | `python3 -I tools/protocol-re/pdb_port.py` |

```bash
P=Files/Client/2017/Fiesta.pdb; T=tools/protocol-re/pdb.py
python3 -I $T $P types '^PROTO_NC_ITEM_CELLCHANGE_CMD$'   # one packet struct, C-like
python3 -I $T $P types '^ABSTATEINDEX$'                   # an enum
python3 -I $T $P publics 'On_NC_MAP_'                     # 2017 client functions (VA, mangled, Class::method)
jq '.opcodes["0x1804"]' docs/protocol/pdb-layouts.json      # flattened layout as the decoders use it
```

## 2. Opcode names

**Table.** For every cmd enum `PROTOCOL_COMMAND_<X>`, the dept is the one whose `NC_<D>_NULL = 0` member it
has (the enum names do not always match the dept: `KINGDOMQUEST` = `NC_KQ` 22, `HOLYPROMISE` = 37,
`CHARACTERTITLE` = `NC_CT` 24, `WEAPONTITLE` = `NC_WT` 23). `LOG_EASY_LOG_SYS` (values ≥ 2000, log codes, no
opcodes) and the empty `MATCH_INSTANCE_DUNGEON` are skipped. Result: **2731 opcodes**. Only
`NC_USER_CONNECTION` (45) and depts without any cmd enum (`AUCTION`, `EVENT_FRIEND`, …) have none.
Six values carry two names (the later one an alias, often a different packet in another direction or link):

| Opcode | First name | Alias | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x082f` | NC_MISC_CONNECTFROMWHERE_DB_REQ | NC_MISC_SERVERPARAMETER_REQ | |
| `0x0830` | NC_MISC_CONNECTFROMWHERE_DB_ACK (9 B) | NC_MISC_SERVERPARAMETER_ACK (3 B: `shoutlevel` u8, `shoutdelay` u16) | 2016 zone uses the 3-byte one (Z01 layout) |
| `0x10d2` | NC_CHAR_FREESTAT_SET_DB_ACK | NC_CHAR_SINGLE_OPTION_CMD | 2016 handler = FREESTAT |
| `0x181f` | NC_MAP_MULTY_LINK_CMD (73 B, S→C) | NC_MAP_MULTY_LINK_SELECT_REQ (12 B, C→S) | |
| `0x244a` | NC_BAT_PKINPKFIELD_WMS_CMD (10 B) | NC_BAT_REALLYKILL_CMD (4 B) | 2016 zone sends 4 B (REALLYKILL), WM handler named PKINPKFIELD |
| `0xac2c` | NC_DICE_TAISAI_TIMER_CMD (7 B) | NC_DICE_TAISAI_DB_ITEM_ID_CHANGE_REQ (32 B) | 2016 zone sends 32 B |

`pdb-layouts.json` keeps the alias layouts in `alts`; the decoders pick the one whose size fits the payload.

**Ranking in `catalog.py`** (name source `pdb2017`): verdict file > C01 `client` name > 2016 `handler`
string > `pdb2017` > send-site log literal > `inferred(REQ+1)`. Each catalog entry whose name differs from
the PDB carries the official name in a `pdb2017` field. Result for the 2572 opcodes of the 2016 binaries:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| unnamed before, now named by the PDB | 1438 |
| 2016 name agrees with the PDB (incl. aliases) | 970 |
| conflict with a 2016 `handler` string | 51 (49 → PDB, 2 kept, table below) |
| conflict with a weak 2016 name (REQ+1 guess, log literal) | 59 (all → PDB by rank) |
| 2016 opcode not in the 2017 enums | 54 (11 in dept 45 `NC_USER_CONNECTION`; most others are noise such as `0x0004`, `0xffff`) |
| 2017 opcode not seen in the 2016 binaries | 213 (not added to the catalog) |

`opcodes.json` now: 1788 `pdb2017`, 726 `handler`, 8 `client`, 1 `inferred(REQ+1)`, 49 unnamed.
The conflicts are scattered (no per-dept cmd shift), so a PDB name at the same value is a good default; it
is still *(pdb2017)* until the item that owns the opcode reads its 2016 code.

Why the 2016 handler strings lose so often: they are profiler/log strings typed by hand inside the handler.
29 of them are copy-pasted from a neighbouring handler (the same string sits in two different 2016 handlers
and the PDB agrees with the other one), others have typos (`CHATC_OLOR`, `ZONE__DONE`), the wrong dept
(`NC_MISC_DB_UI_STATE_SAVE_REQ` on a CHARSAVE opcode) or are shared by one handler registered for several
opcodes (`NC_ITEMDB_BUYFAIL_ACK` on `0x340c/0x340f/0x3492/0x3495`).

## 3. Packet layouts (`pdb-layouts.json`)

Format: `opcodes[op] = {name, aliases?, struct, struct_alias?, size, variable, fields: [[off, type, name, note]], alts?}`
plus `structs[name] = {size, fields}` for array element types. Types follow `annotations.json` (`u8 u16 u32
u64 i8 … f32`, `char[N]` strings, `u8[N]` bytes, `Struct[N]`). Rules:

- Nested structs are flattened with dotted names (`shape.hairtype`); arrays of structs reference `structs`.
- Bitfields sharing a unit become one field `a|b|c`, note `bits a:2@0, b:5@2, …`.
- Unions: name unions (`Name5`, `Name256Byte`, `ORToken`) → `char[N]`; unions with a whole-size primitive
  (`SHINE_ITEM_REGISTNUMBER` → `u64`, `ITEM_INVEN` → `u16`) → that primitive; others → `byte[N]` with the
  alternatives in the note (`SHINE_ITEM_ATTRIBUTE`, `shapedata`).
- A trailing `T[0]` array is variable: its dimension is the nearest earlier integer field whose name contains
  num/cnt/count/len/size (`content[len]`, `ItemArray[ItemCmd.numofitem]`), else `rest` (14 cases).
  The count field is a **guess by name**. `variable` is also set when an element struct has a variable tail.
- Empty structs (C++ `sizeof` 1) are documented as size 0 (212 opcodes).
- `struct_alias`: 47 `NC_CHAR_CLIENT_*` / `NC_CHAR_ZONE_*` opcodes have no own struct; the base struct
  (`PROTO_NC_CHAR_BASE_CMD` for `NC_CHAR_CLIENT_BASE_CMD`) is used *(inferred)*.
- 2483 of 2731 opcodes have a struct; most without one are empty packets in 2017.

**Prefixes (official names).** The 6-byte "ref" prefix of server-internal packets about a player
(`docs/knowledge/Z01.md`) is `struct NETPACKETZONEHEADER { ushort clienthandle; ulong charregistnumber; }`.
In 2017 some structs include it as a member (`PROTO_NC_MISC_CONNECTFROMWHERE_DB_ACK.ToZoneAck.netpacketzoneheader`),
most do not, so a PDB offset is then 2016 offset − 6. The 2-byte prefix (W01 `0x0c13`) is
`struct NETPACKETHEADER { ushort clienthandle; }`, a member of some structs (`PROTO_NC_USER_PASSWORD_CHECK_REQ`).

**Consumers** (all prefer a hand annotation, then the PDB layout, then the generated guess):
- `packets.py`: a "2017 PDB layout" table under each client-facing packet without a hand annotation, with a
  ⚠ when the 2016 length check / send size does not fit.
- `pcap_decode.py`: source `pdb2017`, fields tagged `(pdb2017)` in `.decoded.txt`.
- `make_dissector.py`: table `F.PDB`, "Layout source" `pdb2017` in Wireshark.
- Both decoders now accept dotted count names (`u8[a.num]`) and, when the count is unknown, take as many whole
  elements as the payload holds (was: bytes left, which overran for multi-byte elements).

## 7. Ghidra project `client2017`

Imported headless with the PDB applied (`PdbUniversalAnalyzer.setPdbFileOption` in the pre-script
`tools/protocol-re/SetPdb.java`; the PDB Universal analyzer does not find `Fiesta.pdb` next to `Fiesta.bin`
by itself because of the `.bin` extension):

```bash
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home; R=$PWD; T=$R/tools/protocol-re
G=/opt/homebrew/opt/ghidra@12.1.4/libexec/support/analyzeHeadless
# 1. import + analysis (~5 min) + functions.tsv; saves the project
$G re-data/ghidra client2017 -import Files/Client/2017/Fiesta.bin -loader PeLoader -overwrite -scriptPath $T \
  -preScript EnableParamId.java -preScript SetPdb.java $R/Files/Client/2017/Fiesta.pdb \
  -postScript ExportFuncs.java $R/re-data/exports/client2017 -analysisTimeoutPerFile 7200 > re-data/exports/client2017/ghidra.log 2>&1
# 2. decomp.c + strings.tsv from the saved project (slow: ~200 functions/min with the PDB types, ~2.5 h)
$G re-data/ghidra client2017 -process Fiesta.bin -noanalysis -readOnly -scriptPath $T \
  -postScript ExportAll.java $R/re-data/exports/client2017 > re-data/exports/client2017/export.log 2>&1
```

`decomp.c` of the 2017 export carries the real names (classes, methods, static functions), so a 2017
function is a readable reference for the matching 2016 one: find it by name in `client2017`, then the 2016
address via `names/client/C02.json`.

## 8. 2016 client function names ported from 2017

`python3 -I tools/protocol-re/pdb_port.py [-v]` writes `tools/protocol-re/names/client/C02.json`
(**16702** 2016 client functions; all *(pdb2017)*, names as `Class::method`). It never overwrites a C01 name.

| Pass | How | Names |
|---|---|---|
| 1 opcode | 2016 handler of an opcode (C01 `client-handlers.json`) ← 2017 `Scene::On_NC_*` / `Task::Recv_NC_*` / `On_Recv_NC_*` of the same opcode value, same scene class first; only if the two function sizes are within 25 % (else the 2016 `func` is a helper the 2017 `On_*` wraps; 52 dropped) and the 2016 function is not shared by several 2017 handlers (16 "folded", below) | 713 |
| 2 bytes | first 96 bytes with E8/E9 targets and image-range dwords masked, unique in both builds, sizes within 25 % (Ghidra sizes from `functions.tsv`) | 12539 |
| 3 calls | callees at the same call position in matched pairs with equal call counts, only when all votes agree and sizes are similar; iterated | 3450 |

Checks: of the opcode matches that also have a unique byte match, 316 agree and 3 disagree (bytes win:
`FUN_006614c0` = `User::SetMainCharShapeData`, `FUN_007283e0` = `CQuest::Recv_NC_QUEST_CLIENT_SCENARIO_DONE_ACK`,
`FUN_0072fd00` = `CGuildWar::Add`). All 34 C01 names correspond to their 2017 names in meaning (list in §9).
2016 strings of the form `Class::Method` in a named function: 76 agree, 20 name an inlined callee or a data
member (`NiDX9Renderer::Do_BeginUsingRenderTargetGroup` logs `BeginUsingRenderTargetGroup`); no wrong match seen.
786 of C01's 810 handler functions are now named, 718 of them `On_/Recv_NC_*`.
820 names carry a `_<addr>` suffix: one 2017 name matched two 2016 functions (overloads share a name without
signature; template instances).

## 9. Follow-ups per item

**C01** (client inventory)
- 645+ client-handled opcodes now have official names in `opcodes.json`; regenerate `client-handlers.json`
  names / `docs/knowledge/C01.md` tables from the catalog.
- 34 C01 names have official 2017 counterparts (C02 does not overwrite them), list at the end of §8:
  `X_OnPacket` = `X::ProcessNetMsg` / `X::OnProcessNetMsg`, `ErrorText` = `ErrMsgTable::GetErrMsg`, …
  Rename to the official names (or delete them from C01.json and re-run `pdb_port.py`).
- The `func` of some `client-handlers.json` entries is a helper the 2016 dispatcher calls, not the scene's
  `On_NC_*` method (the 2017 method is a thin wrapper that 2016 inlined): e.g. `FUN_00479fa0` serves 13
  failure opcodes. §8 lists where the byte match disagrees with the opcode match.

**W01** (world manager)
- `0x0c60` NC_USER_RETURN_CHECK_REQ: the hand layout has `userNo u32 @0, handle u16 @4`; the 2016 code
  (`FUN_00419860`: `Pkt_SetOpcode(…, 0xc60, 6)`, u16 `param_1[0x45]` at +0, u32 `param_1[0x49]` at +2) and the
  PDB (`nHandle u16 @0, nUserNo u32 @2`) agree on the opposite order. **Fix the annotation.**
- 7 S2S layouts (`0x0c16 0x0c19 0x101c 0x101d 0x101e 0x104b 0x104c`) match the PDB after the 6-byte
  prefix: name the prefix `NETPACKETZONEHEADER {clienthandle, charregistnumber}` and take the PDB field names.
- `0x0c13` NC_USER_AVATARINFO_ACK: 2016 starts with a 2-byte `NETPACKETHEADER` (`handle`), then `numofavatar`,
  then `PROTO_AVATARINFORMATION[]`; confirm on which link the prefix exists.
- Names: `0x0871` → NC_MISC_ITEMSHOP_URL_DB_ACK, `0x1409` → NC_AVATAR_ERASEDATAFAIL_ACK,
  `0x10d2` keeps NC_CHAR_FREESTAT_SET_DB_ACK (alias NC_CHAR_SINGLE_OPTION_CMD).
- `AVATAR` unknown fields: names in §5.

**L00** (login, `docs/pseudocode/login-server.md`)
- `0x0C5A` = `PROTO_NC_USER_US_LOGIN_REQ {char sUserName[260]; char sPassword[36]; Name5 spawnapps}`:
  the `unused` u8[4] at 256 is the tail of `sUserName`, `extra` u32[5] is `spawnapps` (20 bytes).
- `0x0C66` = `PROTO_NC_USER_CLIENT_WRONGVERSION_CHECK_ACK`, an empty struct; the 1 byte is C++ `sizeof` of
  an empty struct, not a field.
- `0x0c65` (version check from the client) is NC_USER_CLIENT_VERSION_CHECK_REQ `{char sVersionKey[64]}`;
  `0x0c64` (account server) is NC_USER_SET_RETURN_CMD. Replace "(ours)" names from `opcodes.json`.

**Z01** (zone core)
- `0x0830`: the 3-byte layout (`value1` u8, `value2` u16) is `PROTO_NC_MISC_SERVERPARAMETER_ACK
  {shoutlevel, shoutdelay}` (alias at the same value).
- 6 S2S layouts (`0x0c1a 0x0c31 0x101c 0x101d 0x104b 0x104c`) differ only by the 6-byte
  `NETPACKETZONEHEADER`; `0x0c1a` is NC_USER_CONNECTCUT2WORLDMANAGER_CMD.
- Name conflicts settled for PDB: `0x0865` (NC_MISC_SPAMMER_ZONE_CHAT_BAN_CMD), `0x1095`
  (…PARTNER_INFO_RNG), `0x9884`/`0x9885` (…REWARDSTORAGE_ITEM_INFO_ZONE_RNG / …_REWARD_ZONE_RNG).
- `0x2001` NC_ACT_CHAT_REQ (annotations.json): the unnamed u8 at 0 is `itemLinkDataCount`, `length` is `len`.
- SHN row structs (§6) give official column names for the tables Z01 loads.

**P01 / P03**: done here (PDB source wired in, selftests extended). `pcap_decode.py --selftest` was already
failing before C02 (W01's annotation renamed C01's `user_id` to `userId`); the assert now accepts both.

**Phase 2 items** (Z02–Z10, W02–W04, D01–D05): before reading a handler, look up `PROTO_<name>` with
`pdb.py types` and the size row in §4; use the 2017 client function of the same name (`client2017` export)
as a readable reference for the 2016 client side.

## 10. Not reconstructed / uncertain

- Every PDB name or layout is 2017. Only the 51 handler conflicts, `0x0c60`, `0x0830` and the AVATAR struct
  were read in 2016 code here; all other `pdb2017` names/fields are unverified for 2016 by design.
- Variable-array count fields are guessed by name (§3). Arrays of element structs with their own variable tail
  (`PROTO_ITEMPACKET_TOTAL`) decode with the fixed element size, which is wrong for those packets.
- `struct_alias` layouts (47) are inferred.
- Ported client names: byte/call-graph matches between two builds a year apart. Spot checks found no wrong
  match, but a function whose behaviour changed between 2016 and 2017 keeps the 2017 name with 2016 code.
  Read the 2016 body before relying on a ported name for semantics.
- The 70 size differences (§4) are listed, not resolved.
- Kept 2016 names: `0xbc0d` NC_GAMBLE_COIN_USE_VIPCARD_REQ (2017: …VIPCARD_UI_OPEN_REQ) and `0x34cf`
  NC_ITEMDB_MAPLINK_ITEM_COMPARE_MAP_REQ (2017: …RESET_SCROLL_LINK_MAP_INFO_CMD): the handler strings are the
  only 2016 evidence and the behaviour fits them; a 2017 rename cannot be excluded.
